items.title: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
items.summary: The air traffic control system’s overloaded, antiquated telecommunications equipment sustained its latest widespread failure, prompting a call for more money to fuel faster upgrades.

items.title: Flight Canceled During the FAA Ground Stop? Here’s What to Do.
items.summary: Travelers are entitled to refunds if their flights are canceled, regardless of the reason, but airlines won’t guarantee other amenities, such as a hotel room or meal vouchers.

items.title: Nvidia Scandal Prompts Questions of What It Means to Be a Spy
items.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies believe a woman who had an affair with Jensen Huang was a Chinese asset. But there is much more that they are still assessing about her role.

items.title: Why Jensen Huang Was Essential to Nvidia’s Rise
items.summary: Jensen Huang was the driving force at Nvidia, with 60 direct reports and no clear succession plan. Tripp Mickle, one of our technology reporters, examines Mr. Huang’s central role in the company and the artificial…

items.title: Wall Street Loses a Powerful Dealmaker After Nvidia’s CEO Is Ousted
items.summary: The ousted Nvidia chief executive was the consummate dealmaker leading the trillion-dollar A.I. build out.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Leather Jacket Isn’t Helping Him Right Now
items.summary: The Nvidia founder’s signature look branded him as a maverick. Does that image read differently now?

items.title: Alaska Senate Race Between Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola Still Counting Votes
items.summary: The race between Senator Dan S. Sullivan and Ms. Peltola, a former congresswoman, is the only Senate contest that hasn’t been called.

items.title: A Democrat Wins the Alaska Governor’s Race for the First Time Since 1998
items.summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins made a name for himself as a coalition builder willing to raise alarms about his state’s dire fiscal straits.

items.title: Lauren Boebert Loses Re-election Bid in Colorado House Race to Eileen Laubacher
items.summary: Ms. Boebert’s loss to Eileen Laubacher in a conservative House district represents a significant victory for Democrats.

items.title: Did the Redistricting Wars Backfire on Republicans? In a Word, No.
items.summary: The G.O.P. was able to avoid more House midterm losses — on top of the advantage it already had from gerrymandering.

items.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
items.summary: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history.

items.title: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
items.summary: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

items.title: Stuck on the tarmac without information: Travelers share their ground stop experiences
items.summary: Passengers stuck on airplanes on tarmacs across the country during the FAA ground stop on Friday share their stories.

items.title: What we know about the FAA nationwide ground stop
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration took an extraordinary step Friday afternoon by issuing a nationwide ground stop. No planes are taking off at any airport and millions of passengers are stranded.

items.title: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
items.summary: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.

items.title: Old tech blamed for the ground stop that caused flight chaos: 'It got overloaded'
items.summary: The nationwide ground stop that paralyzed the U.S. aviation system on Friday has ended, according to Federal Aviation Administration.

items.title: With his challenge to Schumer, Van Hollen forces a debate over Democrats' mandate
items.summary: Democrats say they have a mandate to deliver change, but as the party gets ready to retake the majority in both the House and Senate, there are divides over who should lead it.

items.title: The government says it will close a beloved D.C. park Sunday. Will a judge step in?
items.summary: Federal judge Ana Reyes grilled the government on Friday about its plans for East Potomac Park, and indicated she could order it to remain open despite President Trump's renovation wishes.

items.title: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
items.summary: President Trump says the "status quo" is what Gulf Arab allies want as the Iran war hits a stalemate and the U.S. midterms force a pivot from threats of attacks to economic pressure.

items.title: The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
items.summary: Election officials are preparing for the Trump administration's pressure tactics over potential noncitizens on state voter rolls to continue, though recent court rulings pose new obstacles.

items.title: U.S. loses measles-elimination status, erasing a landmark public health achievement
items.summary: The finding follows a resurgence that began with a major outbreak in West Texas in January 2025 and was followed by sustained outbreaks in Utah, Arizona and other states.

items.title: FAA lifts ground stop at U.S. airports, leaving travel chaos
items.summary: Thousands of aircraft were halted for more than four hours because of a “temporary telecommunications outage.” Officials were searching for the cause.

items.title: For weeks, Brooklyn residents felt the shaking. Then came a deadly collapse.
items.summary: Eight people were killed, prompting investigations and renewed scrutiny of building-code enforcement.

items.title: Tanker strike sinks cruise ship in New Orleans, plunging passengers into river
items.summary: The incident sent 32 people to hospitals, but officials said there appear to be no fatalities.

items.title: Former death row inmate Richard Glossip pleads guilty to lesser charge
items.summary: The plea agreement is the latest twist in a decades-long saga that at one point led Oklahoma to review its lethal injection protocols.

items.title: Supreme Court to review Trump policy blocking asylum seekers at border
items.summary: The case is the latest immigration issue the justices will weigh in the coming months.

items.title: Trump’s top economic advisers clash over Lutnick’s handling of Nvidia
items.summary: The Commerce Department had been investigating if Megaspeed, the company at the heart of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s spy-sex scandal, breached U.S. export restrictions.

items.title: Woman in truck that crashed into soccer field, killing 2, won’t face charges
items.summary: The woman was napping in her truck before the vehicle jumped a curb and sped onto the field, officials said.

items.title: The story behind the viral ad that helped Scott Colom win in Mississippi
items.summary: Ryan Sayles never had worked on a political campaign before producing the “Pick Another Protein” ad, which ricocheted across the country and internet.

items.title: Oregon school carefully welcomes students back after classroom shooting
items.summary: A nonprofit from South Carolina guided the school district in Bend in best practices to deal with trauma after the deaths of three children and a teacher.
